overall: The AG found the Wareham Board of Sewer Commissioners violated the Open Meeting Law by listing insufficiently specific topics on its August 10 and August 24, 2023 meeting notices; it declined to find the violations intentional and ordered future compliance.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the notice for the first August 10 Board meeting was insufficiently specific.
allegations.key_passage: the topic “47 Sandwich Road,” without any additional information, did not provide sufficient notice to the public that the Board would discuss whether to approve the conversion of a commercial building to a residential building.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the notice for the second August 10 Board meeting was insufficiently specific, including the topic 'work-shop business'.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the topic “work-shop business” was insufficient to inform the public of the anticipated nature of the discussions.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the notice for the August 24 Board meeting was insufficiently specific, citing topics such as 'Narrows Main, resubmit RFP' and 'Bourne'.
allegations.key_passage: we find that they were insufficient to inform members of the public unfamiliar with the regular matters before the Board of the anticipated nature of the Board’s discussions.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged that the notice violations were intentional; the AG considered whether the violations were intentional under G.L. c. 30A, § 23(c).
allegations.key_passage: We have not previously warned the Board against the violation found here, nor do we find other evidence that would support a finding of an intentional violation.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaint; the AG took the opportunity to remind the Board of the requirement to keep accurate minutes that summarize discussions.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law (G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25).
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
